authoring.line: - **An agent authors through the SDK.** `vault.skills.put(folder)`, `vault.packs.put`, `vault.lenses.put`, `vault.agents.put`, `vault.artifacts.put`, with `.fork(h)`, `.archive(h)` and `.export(h)` beside them, and `vault.skills.restoreDefaults()` as the one re-import verb. A folder written on the mount is the same op ([ARCH-0051](/oneiron/surfaces/oneiron-arch-0051-graph-fs-lens/)). Owner, 2026-09-22.

mount.verbLine: There is one verb. `mount(ref)` takes a reference, and the reference is a live head, a fork hash or a repo snapshot. The snapshot kind is CODE's own `repo_ref` discriminator ([ARCH-0002](/oneiron/core/oneiron-arch-0002-structural-entities/) code:D2). The three are one set, so a caller learns one verb for memory and for code. RD-13 ruled this on 2026-09-16. Graph-FS leaves the lens class and becomes the mount. [ONE-1187-D5](/oneiron/core/oneiron-arch-0040-write-gates-provenance-trust-v1/) keeps governing generated read lenses word for word, and ONE-1183-D2 holds here: one file is one op.
mount.rootsLine: A folder written under `skills/`, `packs/`, `agents/` or `lenses/` on the mount is the same put the SDK's `vault.<kind>.put(folder)` makes: the engine hashes the folder on save and lands the entity Candidate or Active as [ARCH-0053](/oneiron/agents/oneiron-arch-0053-skills-agent-self-knowledge-v1/) rules. One op, two doors; the mount is the file face of the vault root (owner, 2026-09-22).
